title: Affirmative possession with singular owners
summary: Build singular-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
objectives: Build singular-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build singular-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
Choose minulla, sinulla, and hänellä from the intended owner. Put on after the owner, then the noun in its basic singular form.
keyPoints: Build singular-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.

steps: First put minulla in the owner position. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with auto (“car”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put sinulla in the owner position. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with pallo (“ball”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put hänellä in the owner position. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Next put on after the owner: “has”.
End with kynä (“pen”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put minulla in the owner position. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with peli (“game”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.

commonMistakes: Begin the requested statement with the owner, then on, then the thing: Minulla on pallo.
Keep the owner form and verb separate: minä names a subject; minulla on says what I have.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “I have a pen.” Start with the owner. Use minulla (“I as the owner”) and kynä (“a pen”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form.
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Affirmative possession sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses fixed on with minulla, sinulla and hänellä.
kynä stays in its basic singular form: one pen.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Translate “Sinulla on peli.” into English. Address one person.
practiceExercises.explanation: Sinulla identifies the person addressed as the owner; fixed on expresses possession.
